La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Post-2000 Arena-Filling Bands Rarity
facts.body: It has become exceptionally difficult for rock bands to emerge since 2000 and achieve the status of arena headliners. Aside from a few exceptions like Arcade Fire, Muse, Linkin Park (though no longer active), and Jack White/The White Stripes, names quickly run out, making Imagine Dragons a rare success story from that era. "Name all the rock bands who have emerged since 2000, who are capable of filling an arena as a headliner today."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: rock

facts.title: Inability to Rebound Post-2000
facts.body: The recorded music industry has largely failed to create new superstar rock acts since the turn of the century, contrasting with previous decades when numerous rock bands could fill arenas and stadiums. This decline is attributed to the breakdown of old industry models, which prioritized physical music sales and allowed for longer artist development. "The recorded music industry has done a terrible job of creating new superstar acts since the beginning of the century."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Barcelona Show Cancellation and Sibling Brawl (2000)
facts.body: On May 20th, 2000, an Oasis show in Barcelona was canceled because drummer Alan White suffered from severe tendonitis. During the band's unplanned downtime, Liam Gallagher made a derogatory remark about Noel's then-wife, Meg Matthews, questioning the paternity of their daughter, Anais. This led to Noel physically assaulting Liam, punching him in the face, splitting his lip, and delivering a serious headbutt, before declaring he quit the band. "At some point in the evening, Liam said something nasty about Null's then-wife Meg Matthews. Let's just say that he questioned the paternity of Null's daughter, Anase. This was a bad idea. Null leapt on Liam, punched him in the face, split his lip, and then gave him a serious headbutt."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Noel's Temporary Departure (2000)
facts.body: After a physical altercation with Liam Gallagher in Barcelona, Noel Gallagher quit Oasis, leading the band to perform 18 subsequent shows without him. A replacement guitarist, Matt Deighton, played with the band in Milan on May 30th. Noel eventually returned on July 15th for UK outdoor festivals, though a press release stated he would no longer tour overseas with the band. "Null did not return to the band until July 15th when it was time to play some big outdoor festivals across the UK. And even then, a press release said that Null would no longer tour with a waste overseas."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Barcelona Concert Cancellation & Paternity Question (2000)
facts.body: On May 20, 2000, Oasis was scheduled to perform in Barcelona, but the show was cancelled because drummer Alan White suffered from severe tendonitis in his hands and arms. This unexpected downtime led to significant drinking among the band members. During this period, Liam Gallagher made a disparaging comment about Noel Gallagher's then-wife, Meg Matthews, specifically questioning the paternity of their daughter, Anais. "On May 20th of that year, Oasis was supposed to perform in Barcelona. However, there was a problem. Former Alan White had bad tendonitis in his hands and arms, which is a very common thing for drummers. And there was no choice but to cancel the show."

facts.title: OCD-Induced Fall and Hip Fracture (December 2000)
facts.body: On December 30, 2000, Joey Ramone, who had struggled with obsessive-compulsive disorder since childhood, was overcome by an intense urge to check if he had properly closed a door across town. Despite fighting the compulsion, his OCD demanded action, leading him to venture out on a cold, icy New York City day. During his journey, he slipped and fell, fracturing his hip due to bones weakened and brittle from chemotherapy treatments for lymphoma. "On December 30, 2000, he was overcome with a feeling that he hadn't closed the door properly on the other side of town." "On his way to that door, wherever it was, Joey slipped and fell."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Ramones

facts.title: Cancer Recurrence Post-Surgery (December 2000 - April 2001)
facts.body: The severe hip fracture Joey Ramone sustained necessitated surgery, which required him to be taken off his anti-lymphoma medication. This interruption caused his lymphoma to come out of remission, ultimately preventing him from ever returning home from the hospital. "And for that, he needed to be taken off his anti-limfoma meds. The lymphoma came out of remission, and Joey wasn't ever able to go home again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Ramones

facts.title: Decision to Break Up (2000)
facts.body: In October 2000, Billy Corgan made the decision to disband the Smashing Pumpkins. Despite their status as one of the most important, influential, and bestselling bands of the 1990s alternative nation, the band faced too many problems with their record label, management, and reportedly with guitarist James Iha, whom Corgan seemed to hold responsible for the ultimate breakup.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.name: The Smashing Pumpkins

facts.title: Final Concert at The Metro (2000)
facts.body: The Smashing Pumpkins' final show was announced on October 17, 2000, and took place on December 2nd at The Metro in Chicago. This club held significant history for the band, as it was also the venue where they played their first proper gig on October 5, 1988. The farewell performance was an emotional night that lasted four long hours, serving as a "grand finale" to their career.

facts.title: Roskilde Festival Tragedy (2000)
facts.body: On June 30, 2000, Pearl Jam performed at the Roskilde Festival in Denmark during its second day, following heavy rains that left 100,000 attendees soaked and safety concerns that led other bands like The Verve and Pet Shop Boys to cancel. During Pearl Jam's 11:30 PM set, a crowd surge pushed attendees against a steel barrier down a slight, muddy incline. Vocalist Eddie Vedder repeatedly stopped the band, imploring the crowd to move back as the crush became a "slow-motion avalanche of bodies." Ultimately, 26 people were injured, and 8 bodies were pulled from the pile, with another person dying later in hospital. The victims were from Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, and Sweden. "Our lives will never be the same, but we know that this is nothing compared to the grief of the families and friends of those involved."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Band's Devastation and Absolution (2000)
facts.body: The tragedy at Roskilde left Pearl Jam devastated, prompting them to consider breaking up permanently. Despite the band's initial anguish, multiple investigations in the following months absolved Pearl Jam of all wrongdoing, negligence, and culpability for the incident. "In the end, though, Pearl Jam was absolved of all wrongdoing, all negligence and all culpability."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Roskilde Festival Tragedy (June 30, 2000)
facts.body: On Friday, June 30, 2000, during Pearl Jam's performance at the Roskilde Festival in Denmark, a crowd surge towards the stage led to a catastrophic crush. Despite Eddie Vedder and the band pleading with the audience to move back, nine people died and countless others were injured when a customized padded barrier failed. This event became one of Europe's worst concert tragedies, leading to the cancellation of the rest of the festival and a police investigation. Pearl Jam fully cooperated, was exonerated from criminal charges, but seriously considered quitting the band due to immense guilt. "nine people died in the crush and countless other suffered injuries making it one of Europe's worst ever concert tragedies."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Roskilde Festival Crowd Crush (June 30, 2000)
facts.body: At approximately 10:30 PM on June 30, 2000, 30 minutes into Pearl Jam's set at the Roskilde Festival in Denmark, a group of people fell in a specific area, destabilized by crowd waves on the rain-slicked, muddy ground. This created a void that quickly filled with bodies, leading to the suffocation of nine people within five minutes. In total, nine people died, and 26 were injured, three seriously, with no evidence of drug or severe alcohol use among the victims. "About 30 minutes into the show, a bunch of people fell down all in one specific area, knocked off balance by waves undulating through the crowd on the rain slick muddy ground."

facts.title: Warped Tour Re-energization (2000)
facts.body: Despite initially refusing ("never, ever play the Warped Tour"), Green Day agreed to join the 2000 Warped Tour after organizer Kevin Lyman offered them a chance to play "with no pressure," hang out with new bands, absorb their energy, and embrace their role as elder statesmen. Playing the tour re-energized the band, introduced them to a new generation of fans, and was pivotal to their career's "second act." "Look, said organizer Kevin Lehmann, here's a chance for you to play some shows with no pressure, hang with the new bands, absorb some of their energy, maybe bask in your role as the elder statesman of this community."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Green Day

facts.title: Career Revival (Circa 2000)
facts.body: Around 2000, Green Day's career was perceived to be in decline, with a general consensus that they had exhausted their creative ideas. However, a successful tour opening for Blink 182 and the strong sales of a greatest hits album released by their label encouraged them to continue and create new music, leading to the "Cigarettes and Valentines" project. "Around 2000, Green Day was in trouble. The general consensus was that they had played out their string. They had nothing new to offer and people were tired of what they were selling. As sort of a last ditch, what the hell effort they went on tour as the opening act for Blink 182, who was really hot at the time. That tour went really, really well. A greatest hits album was released by their label and it sold really, really well."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Third Wave (2000-2010)
facts.body: The third wave of emo, occurring in the early 2000s, represented "peak emo." It began around 2000, peaked around 2008, and started moving into the background by 2010. This period saw emo blow up into the mainstream and fragment into numerous variations, much to the annoyance of purists who often declared "that's not emo." "Third wave emo begins in 2000 and proceeds starting in about 2008 and moved into the background again as of around 2010. This is when things not only began to blow up in the mainstream but also splinter into a million different variations, something that really annoyed the purists. Forgive them if they screamed, that's not emo, about a bunch of acts that were being labeled emo."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Zack de la Rocha Quits (2000)

facts.title: Zack de la Rocha's Departure and Return (2000, 2007)
facts.body: Zack de la Rocha left Rage Against the Machine in the fall of 2000 to pursue solo work, but faced challenges finding inspiration for a full album. The band later reunited in 2007 and has continued to perform through a series of live gigs, demonstrating their enduring presence despite de la Rocha's earlier departure. It all worked out well, though. Rage got back to you there in 2007 and had been holding it together through a series of live gigs ever since."

facts.title: Rhyme and Reason Tour Cancellation (2000)

facts.title: Napster Lawsuit (2000-2001)
facts.body: Metallica initiated a public $10 million lawsuit against Napster after discovering an unreleased demo, "I Disappear," and their entire catalog on the peer-to-peer file-sharing network. The lawsuit was for a minimum of $10 million, or $100,000 per infringed song, whichever was greater. "They fired off a $10 million lawsuit at Napster, very, very public."

facts.title: Napster Lawsuit (2000)
facts.body: On April 13, 2000, Metallica filed a lawsuit against Napster, accusing the platform of aiding and abetting the theft of their music. This action was taken after the band discovered an unauthorized, unreleased demo of their song "I Disappeared" circulating widely on the Napster network. "So on April 13, 2000, the band filed a lawsuit against Napster for aiding and abetting in the theft of their music."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock
facts.name: Metallica

facts.title: Lawsuit Against Napster (2000)
facts.body: Metallica, notably with drummer Lars Ulrich as the public face, filed a lawsuit against Napster on April 30, 2000, after discovering their unreleased demo "I Disappear" and their entire catalog were being freely traded online. Lars Ulrich physically delivered a 60,000-page list of 335,435 alleged Metallica song pirates to Napster's offices. The band sought at least $10 million in damages, a ban for all users trading Metallica songs, and university crackdowns on student downloading. This action generated intense fan backlash, damaging Metallica's reputation as "rich rock stars, bullying fans." Despite this, Napster was ultimately shut down in July 2001 after settling with Metallica and Dr. Dre, confirming that its practices violated copyright. "On April 30, 2000, they made a big deal of launching a lawsuit with drummer Lars Alrich becoming the face of the proceedings."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Hip Break Incident (2000)
facts.body: On December 30, 2000, while walking down a street in New York City, Joey Ramone fell and broke his hip. This severe injury necessitated taking him off his chemotherapy treatment so he could undergo surgery.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 9
facts.name: Joey Ramone

facts.title: Accidental Hip Fracture (December 30, 2000)
facts.body: On a cold and icy December 30, 2000, Joey Ramone, compelled by an OCD urge, slipped and fell on the ice while crossing the city, breaking his hip. His bones had been made brittle by his ongoing chemotherapy treatments, exacerbating the injury. "On December 30, 2000, he was overwhelmed with a feeling that he hadn't closed a door on the other side of the city...Joey slipped and fell on the ice...he broke his hip."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Joey Ramone

facts.title: Cessation of Lymphoma Treatment (December 2000)
facts.body: The hip surgery required after Joey Ramone's fall necessitated a halt to his lymphoma treatments. This interruption caused the disease to come out of remission, making it untreatable and leading to his eventual death. "This required surgery. And that required he stopped his lymphoma treatments. The disease came out of remission and couldn't be beaten back."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Joey Ramone

facts.title: Hip Fracture and Cancer Complications (2000-2001)
facts.body: On December 30th, 2000, while undergoing chemotherapy for lymphoma, Joey slipped on ice outside his building due to his poor vision and broke his hip. This injury necessitated the temporary cessation of his immune-system-weakening cancer drugs for surgery. He was briefly discharged in February 2001 but soon returned to the hospital, never again returning to his apartment. The lymphatic cancer aggressively attacked his immune system, leaving him vulnerable to infection. "On December 30th, 2000, after moving home during some chemotherapy sessions for his lymphoma, he left his building and didn't see the ice on the sidewalk. He slipped, he fell, and he broke his hip. As a result, doctors had to take him off his cancer-fighting drugs, drugs that weakened his immune system so he could undergo surgery for this badly broken hip. He was released for a few days in February, but he was soon back in the hospital. He never went back to his apartment again. The lymphatic cancer then went after Joey's immune system, but he was all but shutting it down and leaving him susceptible to infection."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Early 2000s Revival (2000-2001)
facts.body: The "Post-Punk Revival," also known as the Indie Rock Revival, occurred around 2000-2001. This movement presented a new take on earlier alt-rock, garage rock, and punk styles, bringing sharp and clever new bands to the forefront. "We call this the Indie Rock Revival, or Post-Punk Revival."

facts.body: The Pet Shop Boys cancelled their set at the Roskilde Festival on June 30, 2000, sharing concerns that the organizers were not adequately prepared or had their "act together" given the challenging conditions, including heavy rain and mud.
